description:
Remaq Supply Chain is a young company specializing in one-stop supply chain services for overseas customers, providing sourcing, purchasing, and supply chain management services for cross-border e-commerce sellers, importers, and offline retailers around the world.
We are seeking a highly motivated and proactive Sourcing Specialist to join our team. The ideal candidate will have strong supplier development and negotiation skills, a deep understanding of Chinese manufacturing ecosystems, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, results-driven environment. This role is key to expanding our supplier base, ensuring product quality and cost competitiveness, and supporting the company's business growth.
Key Responsibilities:
Supplier Development & Management
Identify, evaluate, and onboard new suppliers in China across relevant product categories.
Develop and maintain strong, long-term relationships with suppliers to ensure stable supply, competitive pricing, and consistent quality.
Regularly assess supplier performance in terms of price, quality, delivery, and service.
Sourcing & Procurement Support
Handle sourcing requests from overseas clients, including product research, quotation comparison, and sample coordination.
Negotiate pricing, payment terms, lead times, and other commercial conditions with suppliers.
Coordinate with internal teams to ensure smooth order execution from PO to delivery.
Market & Product Research
Stay updated on market trends, product innovations, and pricing dynamics within relevant categories.
Provide sourcing insights and recommendations to support business development and customer solutions.
Risk Control & Compliance
Ensure suppliers meet compliance, quality, and ethical standards.
Identify potential supply chain risks and propose mitigation strategies.
Requirements:
Bachelor's degree or above, preferably in International Trade, Supply Chain, Business, or related fields.
Minimum 2 years of experience in sourcing, purchasing, or supplier development, ideally with exposure to Chinese suppliers.
Strong knowledge of manufacturing processes and supply markets in China.
Excellent negotiation, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Fluent in Chinese (Mandarin) and English, both written and spoken — must be able to communicate directly with Chinese suppliers and international clients.
Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities under tight deadlines.
Self-driven, proactive, and comfortable working in a fast-paced startup environment.
Relevant education in business, supply chain, international trade, or a related field is preferred but not required with strong experience.
title: Sourcing Specialist who speak Chinese

Strong written and verbal communication skills in both English and Mandarin.
A proactive team player who is collaborative, adaptable, and eager to learn.

description:
Job Description
We're looking for an experienced sales leader to help us scale in APAC. This is a pivotal role for a leader who combines strategic vision with hands-on execution.
As the Senior Sales Leader, Asia Pacific, you will be responsible for leading the regional go-to-market effort in one of the fastest-growing markets for data infrastructure. You'll have the autonomy to build the team, define the strategy, and drive the revenue needed to fuel our next phase of growth. You will manage complex enterprise deals, develop strategic partnerships, and serve as the face of Hydrolix in the region.
This is an exciting opportunity for a driven sales leader who wants to make a meaningful impact at a well-funded, rapidly growing startup and be part of the company's leadership team. You will be managing a team of Account Executives and Solutions Engineers, supported by the sales development organization.
The ideal candidate will be someone with a demonstrated history of building high-performing sales teams from the ground up in the APAC region, with a particular focus on infrastructure technology.
We're looking for a "player-coach": someone who can build and lead a team while remaining hands-on with key accounts and opportunities.
Key Responsibilities
- Lead and develop the regional sales organization across APAC, including hiring, mentoring, and managing a team of Account Executives and Solutions Engineers
- Own regional revenue targets and drive consistent quarter-over-quarter growth
- Build and manage a robust pipeline of enterprise opportunities across the region
- Develop and execute the regional go-to-market strategy in alignment with company objectives
- Personally engage in strategic deals, executive-level relationships, and key partnerships
- Collaborate with Product, Marketing, and Customer Success teams to ensure customer satisfaction and drive expansion
- Represent Hydrolix at industry events, conferences, and executive briefings
What You'll Bring
- 7+ years of experience in enterprise technology sales, with at least 3 years in a sales leadership role
- Proven track record of building and scaling high-performing sales teams in APAC
- Deep understanding of the data infrastructure market, including data lakes, streaming data platforms, and real-time analytics
- Strong network of enterprise contacts and partners across the APAC region
- Experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise sales cycles
- Excellent communication, negotiation, and presentation skills
- Self-motivated, results-driven, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced startup environment
The successful candidate will be a player-coach: capable of leading and developing the regional sales organization while remaining personally engaged with strategic customers, major opportunities, executive relationships and key partners.
About Hydrolix
Hydrolix is a Portland-based company revolutionizing data infrastructure. We offer a high-performance, cost-effective data lake platform built for massive-scale log data, with real-time streaming and batch ingestion capabilities.
We are a remote-first company with employees across the US, Canada, Europe and APAC. We offer competitive compensation, including equity, and a comprehensive benefits package. Hydrolix values customer focus, innovation, and execution. Our culture is built on the following values:
Integrity: We do the right thing even when no one is watching.
Bias for action: We move fast and deliver results.
Customer obsession: We put the customer first in everything we do.
Intellectual honesty: We value truth over comfort.
Ideal Candidate Profile
- Bachelor's degree in business, computer science, engineering, or a related field; MBA preferred
- Proven success selling infrastructure technology to enterprise customers in APAC
- Experience with consumption-based or SaaS pricing models
- Background in log management, SIEM, CDN analytics, or adjacent infrastructure categories
- Existing senior relationships across APAC enterprise and partner ecosystems

About The Opportunity: We are seeking a Cyber Security Operations Center (CSOC) Analyst with 3-4 years of experience in security monitoring, detection engineering, and incident response to join a lean, high-ownership security team at a cryptocurrency exchange. You will work closely with our MSSP and internal engineering team to close gaps between raw alerting and actual risk reduction — turning threat intel feeds into action, validating that our detections actually work, and helping build out new programs like insider threat monitoring. This is not a pure alert-queue role: you'll be expected to write and improve detection logic, document your work so it survives beyond you, and take ownership of incidents end-to-end rather than handing off after triage.
Responsibilities:
• Perform triage, analysis, and escalation of security alerts across SIEM, EDR/XDR, WAF, email security, and cloud log sources, coordinating with our MSSP where relevant.
• Own incidents end-to-end — triage through resolution through "what changed afterward" — and turn that work into documented playbooks and updated detection logic, not just closed tickets.
• Develop, tune, and validate SIEM detection rules (ES|QL/EQL/KQL or equivalent), including running detection validation exercises against existing use cases to confirm they actually fire.
• Convert threat intelligence feeds and scheduled hunting queries (e.g., lookalike domain alerts, anomalous auth events) from passive detection into defined, actionable response — closing the loop between "we saw it" and "we did something about it."
• Support the build-out of an insider threat monitoring program, including identity and privileged-access anomaly detection.
• Understand our detection tooling and log source pipelines (maintained day-to-day by our MSSP) well enough to confirm they're onboarded correctly and actually working — you're not expected to build or maintain this tooling yourself, but you need to be able to verify it.
• Track and report CSOC performance metrics (MTTD/MTTR, false-positive rates, MSSP SLA adherence) to support continuous improvement of operations.
• Write and maintain operational documentation, playbooks, and detection rule rationale so institutional knowledge isn't concentrated in one or two people.
• Contribute to automation of repetitive triage and enrichment work (scripting, workflow tools) to reduce manual toil across the team.
• Collaborate with internal stakeholders and regional partners, where Chinese language skills may be required.
Requirements:
• Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field.
• 3-4 years of experience in a Security Operations Center (SOC) or equivalent security monitoring/detection engineering role.
• Hands-on experience with SIEM tools, including: 1. Detection rule and use case development, and the ability to reason about whether a rule actually detects what it claims to (detection validation mindset, not just rule-writing). 2. Query/rule-writing experience in ES|QL, EQL, KQL, or equivalent. 3. Alert triage, enrichment, and case management with ticketing systems. 4. Comfort reading raw logs (auth events, CloudTrail-style audit logs, process trees) without relying solely on pre-built dashboards.
• Working knowledge of Python or similar scripting for automation, log parsing, or extending existing tooling — enough to pick up and modify scripts someone else wrote, not build from scratch.
• Knowledge of common attack techniques, malware behavior, and network security principles, with familiarity mapping detections to MITRE ATT&CK.
• Familiarity with incident response frameworks (e.g., NIST, SANS) and a track record of writing playbooks or documentation from real incidents.
• Exposure to identity/IAM log analysis or insider threat / UEBA concepts is a strong plus, given active program build-out.
• Good understanding of cloud security (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and comfort across varied operating systems (Windows, Linux, macOS).
Nice to Haves:
• Familiarity with atomic-level adversary emulation using Atomic Red Team or equivalent framework, for the purpose of validating that detections fire as expected.
• Effective communication and documentation skills.
• Chinese language proficiency (reading, writing, and/or speaking) is a strong advantage.
• Relevant certifications (e.g., CISSP, GCIH, GCFA, CompTIA Security+, CySA+, CEH, or similar) are desirable.
Perks & Benefits:

• Various team-building programs and company events.
• And many more! Apply and let us tell you more!

What We're Looking For (in Order):

• AI-native production: You already produce dozens of generative video/image/voice tools daily, by choice. You can tell us your stack and what each tool is good/bad at.

• A system for markets you don't speak. You've shipped winning creative in languages you don't speak — through native creators, transcreators, and a review layer you built and ran. We're opening more markets; your localization system matters more than any single language.
• Senior player-coach: Roughly 5–8 years in performance creative, growth, or UA creative roles. You want to produce first and manage later — not the reverse.
